parameters.content:
## Employee Onboarding Automation Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: BambooHR, Rippling, Workday or Personio sends a webhook when a candidate's status becomes Hired. A fallback Schedule Trigger polls the HRIS every hour for platforms without webhooks.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - The AI agent answers only from the handbook and cites the page; it refuses pay, performance and grievance topics and routes them to HR.
   - Account provisioning is requested, never executed, by the workflow — IT approves in their own tool.
   - Personal data stays in the HRIS; the workflow passes identifiers, not copies of documents.
   - Every automated message is logged on the hire's board so HR can see exactly what was sent.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/employee-onboarding-automation/
Want it built and run for you? $247/month · custom $3,500–5,000 one-time

nodes.name: Webhook: Receive the new-hire event
nodes.notes:
Receive the new-hire event

The HRIS posts the new employee record: name, role, department, start date, manager, location. The workflow validates required fields and stops with an alert if the record is incomplete.

assignments.name: config.your_name
assignments.value: Your name — signs every outgoing message

assignments.name: config.approver
assignments.value: #approvals — a Slack channel, or an email address

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- HRIS employee record (BambooHR, Rippling, Workday, Personio)
- Role → checklist map (Google Sheet or Notion)
- Employee handbook and policy documents (vector store)
- IT ticketing system (Jira SM, ServiceNow, Freshservice)
- Calendar and email (Google Workspace or Microsoft 365)

nodes.name: Set: Build the checklist for this role
nodes.notes:
Build the checklist for this role

A role → checklist map (kept in a Google Sheet or Notion database so HR can edit it without touching the workflow) defines the tasks, owners and due dates relative to the start date: paperwork, equipment, accounts, training modules, introductions.

nodes.name: Notion: Create the tracking board
nodes.notes:
Create the tracking board

One page per hire with every task, owner and due date. Jira, Asana, ClickUp or a Google Sheet work the same way. This is the single place HR looks.

nodes.name: Google Calendar: Schedule the first two weeks
nodes.notes:
Schedule the first two weeks

Books the manager 1:1, team introductions, IT setup slot and mandatory training from the checklist, inviting the right people with the right context.

nodes.name: Gmail: Run the welcome sequence
nodes.notes:
Run the welcome sequence

Day −7, −1, 1, 7 and 30 emails, personalised from the record: what to expect, who to meet, where things are. Slack or Teams DMs once the account exists.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Answer policy questions" step of the Employee Onboarding Automation Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: A Slack bot backed by an AI Agent node with your handbook in a vector store. It answers PTO, benefits, expenses and equipment questions with citations to the handbook page, and hands anything about pay, performance or complaints to HR.

Rules:
- The AI agent answers only from the handbook and cites the page; it refuses pay, performance and grievance topics and routes them to HR.
- Account provisioning is requested, never executed, by the workflow — IT approves in their own tool.
- Personal data stays in the HRIS; the workflow passes identifiers, not copies of documents.
- Every automated message is logged on the hire's board so HR can see exactly what was sent.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.notes:

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Answer policy questions
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger: Chase overdue tasks and check in
nodes.notes:
Chase overdue tasks and check in

A daily run compares the board to today's date, nudges owners of overdue items, and sends the 30/60/90-day check-in survey to the hire and the manager. Results go on the board.
